profile.reading:
TierPoint operates a data center at 311 Eddy Lane in Franklin, Tennessee, in Williamson County within the greater Nashville metro area, and markets it as one of its more highly certified facilities. The original facility opened in 2013 with 10,000 square feet of raised floor, and TierPoint announced a further 20 million dollar expansion in August 2022, part of a total 45 million dollar campus investment built in partnership with Compass Data Centers, with roughly 20 percent of the new space pre-sold before completion. The current facility spans more than 52,000 total square feet with more than 26,000 square feet of raised floor and 1,300 square feet of business-continuity seating, backed by four 2-megawatt redundant generators. Notably, this is the most highly certified facility in this research batch: TierPoint states the site holds Uptime Institute Tier III certification for design and construction, as well as LEED-Gold certification, in addition to its standard SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II (including HITRUST), HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, and ISO 27001 compliance package. The facility's 2013 opening predates TierPoint's major 2014 through 2016 acquisition wave that brought in Xand, Windstream Hosted Solutions, and Cosentry, suggesting this was an organic TierPoint build rather than an acquired facility, though that was not explicitly confirmed by any source reached this session. TierPoint, headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, now operates roughly 40 data centers across 20 US markets. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed.

TierPoint has also grown through significant recent capital raises beyond its acquisition history: a 320 million dollar equity round in April 2020 led by Argo Infrastructure Partners, Wafra, and Macquarie Capital Principal Finance alongside existing investors, followed by Argo's 500 million dollar investment in February 2022 that made it TierPoint's largest single equity investor, and a further increase to Argo's ownership and capital commitment announced in December 2025. Nashville's data center market has grown considerably in recent years as the broader Tennessee metro has attracted technology-sector investment, and Williamson County specifically has become one of the wealthiest and fastest-growing counties in the state, a factor in the strong pre-leasing TierPoint reported for this campus's 2022 expansion.

reading.body:
This facility publishes no power capacity, limiting any judgment of its scale relative to other Tennessee data centers or its fitness for AI training workloads.

TierPoint operates this 26,000-square-foot colocation site as a suite within a larger building rather than a purpose-built shell, which signals mid-market enterprise demand rather than hyperscale infrastructure. The seven certifications on file, dominated by SOC 1 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, HITRUST, and ITAR, describe a workload profile tilted toward compliance-driven use cases: financial systems under audit control, payment card processing, regulated healthcare data, and export-restricted defense information. ISO 27001 and LEED round out a stack that prioritizes security governance and operational standards over raw capacity.

For AI specifically, this signature matters. Large-scale GPU training requires transparent power density and sustained load capacity, neither of which this facility publishes. The certification portfolio instead suggests inference, data management, or model serving for regulated industries, where compliance overhead exceeds the computational demand of training runs. Tennessee as a whole publishes power figures for only one of twenty-four mapped facilities, making state-level pattern detection impossible. This facility's contribution to the regional AI compute base cannot be assessed from the data available.
